=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Package

**Preliminary points**

- I reviewed all 16 items. The Seller's "[STANDARD]" labels and "reviewer efficiency note" don't mean the Buyer has accepted them, so I haven't treated any item as cleared.
- The "FINAL" and "not to be re-opened" language is the Seller's position, not a binding agreement. The Buyer has not agreed these terms.
- Several known exposures total about **AUD 4.13m** (Riverlark 3.2m, bonuses 0.42m, Ironquay 0.18m, Sandbar 0.33m). That is about 86% of the Seller's proposed AUD 4.8m general cap, before the incident, Bluefen, or Mossvale exposures are counted. Under the Seller's Clause 8.3 and Schedule 7, the Buyer could not recover for these matters at all. They need specific indemnities or price adjustments.
- This is a commercial and legal analysis, not formal NSW legal advice. Specialist input is needed on privacy, tax, and IP.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A materially higher general cap, with known matters carved out to specific indemnities outside the cap. Fundamental warranties at full price.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at a higher general cap (for example 30–50% of price) and carve out known issues.
- **Reason:** AUD 4.8m is already largely consumed by identified exposures, leaving little protection for unknown liabilities.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** A low de minimis, a tipping (first-dollar) basket of about 0.5% of price (around AUD 120,000), and aggregation of related claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible structure. Counter with a tipping basket and related-claims aggregation.
- **Reason:** A deductible means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of loss before any recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims, applied to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** About 36 months for general warranties, and longer for tax (until the assessment period closes plus a buffer). Fundamental and fraud claims on a longer or statutory basis.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 36 months and reject universal application.
- **Reason:** 18 months may not cover a full audit cycle, and the incident and Bluefen issues could surface later.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties capped at full price, with a long or statutory time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to what the Buyer is actually acquiring. Subjecting them to ordinary warranty limits is inappropriate.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Not addressed. The Seller's limitation, exclusive-remedy, and non-reliance language (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) applies to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that fraud, including fraud by Seller officers or employees and wilful concealment, is excluded from all caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, and non-reliance provisions.
- **Recommendation:** Insert an express fraud carve-out. Confirm NSW counsel's view on enforceability of exclusions for fraud.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the Seller's language appears to cover fraud claims, and an express carve-out removes doubt.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers, and public searches (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, against a specific warranty, and fairly disclosed. No general disclosure of the data room or public registers.
- **Recommendation:** Strike general disclosure entirely.
- **Reason:** General disclosure would remove warranty protection for every issue in the data room, including the incident and Bluefen.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No Buyer claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. At most, actual knowledge of named individuals, limited to specific facts disclosed in writing. No constructive or "discoverable" knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Address known issues through specific indemnities or price adjustments.
- **Reason:** A "discoverable" standard turns ordinary diligence into a waiver of warranty rights.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The final consent and clause 11.3 conditions are not in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A condition precedent to Completion requiring a written, unconditional Bluefen consent under clause 11.2, and evidence that all clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Otherwise, the Buyer may terminate or require an escrow or price adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a CP, not a reasonable-endeavours obligation.
- **Reason:** Roughly AUD 3.6m (about 30%) of revenue depends on this consent, and a consent may still carry conditions.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding. Release to be provided after Completion. Not repaid; no discharge of security.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion through the funds flow, with a payout letter and discharge of security (clause 9.2) delivered at Completion. Treated as Debt, deducted from price on the debt-free basis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. Repay at Completion.
- **Reason:** The Buyer should not fund debt that was not priced, and the Company's assets should not remain encumbered after Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses, not in the funds flow. Silent on payroll tax and superannuation.
- **Buyer wants:** Treat the bonuses and all related employer on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, and similar) as Debt or transaction costs, deducted from price and borne by the Seller. Reconcile the funds flow to include them.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct from price and add an indemnity for on-costs.
- **Reason:** On a debt-free basis, these are Seller-economic liabilities, and omitting them from the funds flow would shift the cost to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment. AUD 180,000 is open. No proof of payment or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity covering all Ironquay claims relating to SOW3 and IP ownership, not subject to basket, de minimis, or knowledge. Payment of the AUD 180,000 before Completion or retention from price. A written confirmatory assignment of Project Materials as a CP.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the limited indemnity. Require payment or retention and a confirmatory assignment.
- **Reason:** Clause 7.3 means ownership of the SOW3 materials is not secured until all fees are paid.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident
- **Seller:** Preliminary operational matter, "not expected to be material." Investigation ongoing. About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) may have been exposed to an unintended external address. Unknown whether accessed or whether notification is required.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity covering investigation, notification, regulatory (OAIC), and third-party costs, not subject to cap, basket, or knowledge. Pre-signing forensic review, an investigation covenant with access rights, and privacy counsel review under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), including the notifiable data breaches scheme.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the materiality characterisation. Require the indemnity and forensic review.
- **Reason:** Personal information exposure with unknown access is a live regulatory risk, and notification obligations may fall on the Company after Completion.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 (3 × 110,000), described as ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Copies of the renewal terms, including term length and termination rights. An interim covenant requiring Buyer consent to any renewal outside the ordinary course. Accrued or pre-Completion amounts treated as Debt or working capital.
- **Recommendation:** Obtain the terms and require Buyer consent to renewals.
- **Reason:** The timing, scope, and terminability of these commitments are unclear and could be debt-like.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Collapses all claims into one regime: the same cap, threshold, and time limit for everything (see N-003, N-004, N-005).
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories for general warranties, fundamental warranties (title and capacity), tax, specific indemnities, and fraud. Each with its own cap, threshold, and time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject collapsing the categories.
- **Reason:** A single regime would apply the lowest cap and shortest time limit to the most serious claims.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012, which shows Harbourglass as holder of 100% of shares. The Seller says nothing about the Buyer's own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing, including ASIC company extracts, a certified copy of the register, a PPSR search for security interests, confirmation of no options or convertible instruments, board approval of the transfer, and a fundamental title warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent title searches and verification before signing.
- **Reason:** The register is the Seller's own document. The Buyer needs independent evidence of title and that the shares are unencumbered.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties treated as "settled under the general regime." Actual warranty text not in the package.
- **Buyer wants:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, surviving until the statutory assessment period closes plus a buffer. IP ownership warranties with a separate, higher cap, covering Ironquay and all other developers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require the actual tax and IP warranty text, and treat both as separate categories.
- **Reason:** Applying the general regime would subject tax and IP exposures to the 20% cap and 18-month limit.

---

**Matters outside the 16 items that need attention:** The Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009), the office lease notification obligation (DD-007), and the DD-010 Ironquay balance (verify with bank records, not just the data room) should each be checked for consent or payment requirements before signing.
